title: Counting and Adding Small Numbers
length_note: Ten classes of 8 to 12 minutes each, about 100 minutes in total. Each class teaches one idea, so a learner can stop after any of them and pick up again without losing the thread. Counting to 20 takes three classes: 0 to 10 with objects (10 is new after Numbers 0 to 9), then 11 to 20, then counting out a requested number. More and fewer take two classes, because comparing groups and 'one more or one fewer' are different skills. Adding takes three classes, moving from objects to no objects, so nothing is skipped. Coins and the calendar each get their own short class so that every class stays short. Subtraction is not in the brief, so the course does not teach it. 'One fewer' is covered only as a counting idea.

classes.title: Counting things from 0 to 10
classes.goal: Count up to 10 objects by touching each one once, and say how many there are.
topics: Quick review of numbers 0 to 9
Meeting 10
One touch for each object, one number word for each touch
The last number said tells how many
Counting spoons, cups or buttons

classes.title: Counting from 11 to 20
classes.goal: Say the numbers 11 to 20 in order and count up to 20 objects.
topics: Counting on from 10
Spotting patterns in the number words and written numbers 11 to 20
Counting in small groups to keep your place
Saying numbers aloud and tracing them in the air

classes.title: Counting out a number: setting a table
classes.goal: Count out the number of items asked for, up to 20, such as 6 forks for 6 people.
topics: Counting out versus counting what is already there
Setting a table: one plate, one fork, one cup per person
Checking by counting again
Stopping at the number asked for

classes.title: More and fewer
classes.goal: Look at two groups and say which has more and which has fewer.
topics: Matching items one to one to compare two groups
Words: more, fewer, same
Comparing by counting both groups
Everyday examples such as chairs and people, or socks and shoes

classes.title: One more, one fewer
classes.goal: Say the number that is one more or one fewer than a number from 1 to 10.
topics: Adding one object to a group and recounting
Taking one object away and recounting
Next number up and next number down in the counting order
Connecting one more to the number after

classes.title: Putting groups together (totals to 5)
classes.goal: Join two small groups of objects and say the total, up to 5.
topics: What adding means: putting together
Words: add, and, makes, total
Counting all the objects from 1
Saying '2 and 3 makes 5'

classes.title: Adding with objects up to 10
classes.goal: Add two groups of objects with a total up to 10 and say the number sentence aloud.
topics: Two groups, one total
Counting all, then counting on from the larger group
Using two colours of counters to see the parts
Pairs that make 10, such as 6 and 4

classes.title: Adding without objects
classes.goal: Work out sums within 10 using counting on, fingers or a number line, with nothing to hold.
topics: Starting from the bigger number and counting on
Fingers and a number line as helpers
Picturing the objects in your mind
Reading and saying simple sums, such as 4 + 3
Checking an answer with objects

classes.title: Adding with coins
classes.goal: Count and add small amounts with single-unit coins, with totals up to 10.
topics: Telling coins apart by look and by value
Counting single-unit coins one by one
Adding two small amounts of coins
Checking change in a simple pretend shop
Local coins are different in different countries, so the lesson must use the learner's own currency

classes.title: Counting and adding on a calendar
classes.goal: Use a calendar to count days up to 20 and add a few days to a date.
topics: Finding today's date and counting the days to an event
Counting on from a date, such as 3 days after the 5th
Reading the numbers 1 to 20 in a grid
Calendar layouts differ, such as which day the week starts on, so the lesson must match the learner's calendar
